images.title: Where can the next number go?
images.purpose: Show that the next number in a Hidato must go in one of the 8 cells touching the current cell.
images.composition: One 3 by 3 block of cells in the centre of the frame with the current number in the middle cell, the 8 touching cells highlighted, and one short caption beside it.
exact_structure: 1 block of 3 rows and 3 columns of equal square cells, 9 cells in all
Middle cell: reddish purple #CC79A7 fill with the number '12'
The 8 surrounding cells (4 side cells and 4 corner cells): light teal #0072B2 fill, each with a small grey #6B7280 '?' in it
1 caption to the right of the block: '13 goes in one of these 8 cells'
no arrows and no other numbers in the cells
labels: 13 goes in one of these 8 cells
rejection: a number of highlighted touching cells other than 8, or the corner cells left out
any number in the cells other than 12
more than one cell containing a number
images.takeaway: Each next number sits in one of the 8 cells around the last one, so check side and corner neighbours when filling a gap.
images.description: A 3 by 3 block with 12 in the middle and the 8 touching cells marked with question marks as places for 13.
images.context: Shown beside the practice on solving the Hidato grids.
images.teaching_notes: When stuck, look for a cell with only one open neighbour, since the path is forced there.

image_decisions.why: Highlighting the 8 neighbours makes the adjacency rule easy to apply in the practice grids.
